plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher than my value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $19.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids. Bidding my true value of $44 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid (guaranteeing non-negative profit) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding negative profit). Overbidding risks paying more than my value; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no prior history to exploit, truthful bidding is optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $43 ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay, maximizing expected profit.
